players.product: data-center chillers, BASX custom air handlers & liquid-cooling packages (Redmond / Memphis)

quarterly_data.signal: Fourth consecutive quarterly revenue record: second quarter net sales were a record $627 million, an increase of 101% year-over-year and 26% sequentially; non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased 102.3% to $94.2 million (15.0% margin) and adjusted diluted EPS grew 213.6% to $0.69. Gross margin was 24.3%, down from 26.6%, reflecting the ramp of the Memphis facility, outsourcing and inflation.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 net sales $627 million (+101% YoY, +26% QoQ); adj. EBITDA $94.2 million (+102.3%); adj. EPS $0.69 (+213.6%); gross margin 24.3%

quarterly_data.signal: BASX-branded (data-center cooling) sales were a record, increasing 216% year over year in the quarter and 501% on a two-year stack; for the first half of the year BASX-branded sales were up 137% year over year and 570% on a two-year stack. Management attributes the growth to sustained data center cooling demand, higher production output and greater utilization of recently added manufacturing capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: BASX-branded sales +216% YoY in Q2 (+501% two-year stack); 1H +137% YoY (+570% two-year stack)

quarterly_data.signal: AAON Coil Products segment sales were $146.7 million, up $88.2 million or 151%, driven by $126.6 million in BASX branded liquid cooling product sales, which increased 208% during the quarter; analysts noted liquid cooling was over 85% of that segment. BASX segment sales grew 221% to $218 million with gross margin of 30.0%, up from 27.9%.
quarterly_data.figure: BASX-branded liquid cooling product sales $126.6 million (+208% YoY); BASX segment sales $218 million (+221%), gross margin 30.0%

quarterly_data.signal: Memphis data-center cooling facility is ramping ahead of plan: in Q2 alone the brand-new Memphis site did roughly half of the total year 2025 revenue that BASX did out of Redmond. Memphis overhead impacted the Oklahoma segment by $18.1 million (vs $3 million a year ago); AAON continues to turn on more production lines in Memphis. Capital expenditures total $102.6 million year to date for incremental capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: Memphis Q2 revenue ~half of BASX Redmond full-year 2025; Memphis overhead $18.1 million; YTD capex $102.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog remains nearly double prior year levels despite record conversion; over the prior four quarters data-center bookings had a book-to-bill approaching three. BASX-branded bookings in Q2 were below the unusually elevated levels of recent quarters, which management attributes to lumpiness of large orders (no specific order push out); AAON-branded bookings rose approximately 16% year over year and AAON-branded backlog rose 6% sequentially.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog nearly 2x prior year; trailing-four-quarter data-center book-to-bill approaching three; AAON-branded bookings +16% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook raised to sales growth of 55% to 60% (top line up about 20% vs prior guide), gross margin of 25% to 26%, SG&A of 13% to 14% of sales and D&A of $95 million to $100 million. The guide assumes approximately 20% growth in the AAON brand, which implies BASX will again more than double in the year after 140% growth the prior year, versus an overall data center market growing around 30% - i.e. continued share gain. BASX sales are expected to be flattish quarter-over-quarter in Q3 and Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 sales growth 55% to 60%; gross margin 25% to 26%; BASX to more than double vs data center market ~30%

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline is the strongest it has ever been, with a tremendous amount of high-confidence pipeline with existing customers for 2027 and 2028 deliveries that did not hit the books in Q2; new-customer diversification is spread evenly across liquid cooling, air-side and chiller products rather than concentrated in one product, and management expects BASX backlog to keep building into 2027.

Supply chain: data-center HVAC players face constraints sourcing fans; BASX has manufactured its own fans from the day the business started and AAON insourced plenum fans a couple of years ago, which management calls a competitive benefit, though AAON still buys some fans and sees capacity constraints in the fan market. Management embeds some potential supply-chain impact into the back-half BASX outlook.
